title: PR #47050 added the project-scoped rule snooze (mute) endpoint, which loads the issue/metric alert rule by id alone without scoping it to the project in the URL, so a user can mute alert rules in other organizations.

vulnerable_findings.explanation: The endpoint fetches Rule/AlertRule objects using rule_id directly from the URL without verifying that the rule belongs to the project (or organization) identified in the URL. An attacker can supply a rule_id belonging to a completely different organization's project and potentially snooze it. findings.explanation: All database queries use Django ORM with parameterized lookups (e.g., Rule.objects.get(id=rule_id), RuleSnooze.objects.get_or_create(...)), with no raw SQL construction involving user-controlled input.

The endpoint fetches Rule/AlertRule objects using rule_id directly from the URL without verifying that the rule belongs to the project (or organization) identified in the URL. An attacker can supply a rule_id belonging to a completely different organization's project and potentially snooze it. The authorization check in can_edit_alert_rule only verifies team membership/org membership for the acting user but does not validate that rule.project == project or rule.organization == project.organization. This is a classic IDOR: object fetched by a user-controlled ID without an ownership/scope check.
findings.suggested_fix: Scope the ORM lookup to the current project/organization, e.g. Rule.objects.get(id=rule_id, project=project) and AlertRule.objects.get(id=rule_id, organization=project.organization), to ensure the rule actually belongs to the project/org the caller has access to.
